country.comment: Single-country study of Nigeria examining ethnic/geopolitical zones, states, and local government areas (LGAs).
country.where_found: PDF p. 2, Title, Abstract, Section 1; PDF p. 4, Section 2

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative descriptive trends and cross-sectional OLS reduced-form regression estimates on aggregated DHS (2003–2013 for infrastructure) and Afrobarometer (2012) data.
effect_estimate.value: Between 2003 and 2013, national mean household access rose from .2 (20%) to .5 (50%) for improved sanitation and from .4 to .6 for potable water, while ethnic horizontal inequality (GGini by geopolitical zone) declined from .3 to about .1 for improved sanitation and from .15 to .05 for potable water. In cross-sectional OLS regressions across LGA-ethnic state units (N = 631; Table 4), precolonial political centralization in compliant (non-supermajority Muslim) ethnic states is positively associated with historically federally administered flush toilet access (beta = .059, SE = .026, p < .05; baseline without interaction beta = .039, SE = .019, p < .05), whereas noncompliance/hegemonization under the 1976 Local Government Reform Law (Cent x Supermajority Muslim interaction) offsets this gain (beta = -.055, SE = .029, p < .10). In contrast, for locally administered WASH services (N = 631; Table 5), neither precolonial centralization nor Cent x Supermajority Muslim is statistically significant for improved pit latrines (Cent beta = .008, SE = .045; Cent x S.Mus beta = .007, SE = .064; Supermajority Muslim beta = .181, SE = .065, p < .01), piped water (Cent beta = .014, SE = .037; Cent x S.Mus beta = .033, SE = .038), or tubewell water (Cent beta = .079, SE = .060; Cent x S.Mus beta = -.104, SE = .066). Across LGAs matching 2012 Afrobarometer and 2013 DHS data (Table 7), local government trust and quality are positively associated with locally administered improved pit latrines (trust in local governing council beta = .127, SE = .072, p < .10; cleaning beta = .132, SE = .048, p < .01; health standards beta = .170, SE = .054, p < .01; marketplace maintenance beta = .183, SE = .058, p < .01), negatively associated with federally administered flush toilets (trust beta = -.214, SE = .052, p < .01; cleaning beta = -.124, SE = .049, p < .05; health beta = -.141, SE = .050, p < .01; marketplace beta = -.193, SE = .044, p < .01), and not significantly associated with piped water (betas -.019 to .030, p > .10).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at <= 2 for cross-sectional observational design; rated 1 because the study documents reduced-form statistical associations (explicitly noted by the author as correlations) between historical centralization/1976 Local Government Reform compliance proxies, perceived local government quality, and WASH access without directly observing fiscal/administrative allocation transactions.
